scope: Local verification of the hosted business application: isolated synthetic automated tests and an explicitly recorded owner-assisted live Google sign-in; not public-launch approval

google_sign_in_follow_up.earlier_record_note: The full-suite totals and fingerprints in the sections below describe the earlier verification run, before this callback-diagnostics change.
google_sign_in_follow_up.regression_coverage: Recognized client/code rejections, signing-key failures, redaction of unknown/non-JSON provider payloads, no signing-key request after token-exchange rejection, and unchanged account/identity/web-boundary tests.

initial_live_result.resolution: The owner updated the private server configuration. Mboa was restarted to load it, and a fresh Google sign-in succeeded. No real credential values or provider response bodies are recorded.

latest_live_result.connectivity_checks: After an ERR_ADDRESS_UNREACHABLE screenshot, the public Google sign-in host responded from Windows and its public OpenID configuration loaded in the same VS Code browser. No network or firewall settings were changed.
latest_live_result.evidence: User completed a fresh Google flow and confirmed the workspace opened. Redacted server logs show callback/session/projects success; an independent same-origin browser session request returned authenticated, Google-linked and verified-email flags. Account identifiers, email addresses, secrets, authorization codes and tokens are omitted.
latest_live_result.limitations: One real local sign-in was verified. This does not establish production Google consent/redirect configuration, explicit linking to an existing password account, SMTP delivery, live Gemini behavior or Ubuntu VPS readiness.
